svg.aria-label: Accuracy by version. The four-agent LLM pipeline: llm-v1 73.0 percent and llm-v2 77.1 percent, both scored on 770 questions; llm-v8 81.7 percent on the 349-question unseen gate split. The single Claude session, sdk-v1, 90.5 percent on the same 349 questions. A dashed line marks the 89.4 percent human-expert figure from the ConvFinQA paper, measured on a different split.
svg.title: 73.0% to 90.5%, across four gated versions

g.title: llm-v1 · 73.0% (562 of 770) · the starting prompt set for the four-agent pipeline, bundle t1.p1.r1.c1
llm-v2 · 77.1% (594 of 770) · a GEPA run over DSPy rewrote all four prompts; champion again after the 2026-09-03 rollback, and the baseline of campaign c01

llm-v8 · 81.7% (285 of 349) on the unseen gate split · campaign c01 experiment 3: the teacher blamed the retriever, one prompt changed, +4.58 pp over llm-v2 at one-sided clustered McNemar p 0.040 · the champion the demo serves

sdk-v1 · 90.5% (316 of 349) on the same 349 questions · llm-v8's four prompts distilled into one Claude Agent SDK session on claude-sonnet-5 with the same six calculator tools · +8.88 pp over llm-v8 at p 0.0003 · promoted to sdk_champion, never to champion

human expert 89.4% · Chen et al. 2022, Table 5, measured on the paper's own held-out test set; the 349-question split used here is drawn from the public train pool, so this line is orientation rather than a like-for-like baseline
